name: Lottery & Prize Scams
summary: Notification of a prize you never entered for, released only after you pay a tax, delivery or clearance fee.

typicalLoss.note: Fees escalate steadily, and victims often pay several before accepting the prize does not exist.

targets: Anyone reachable by SMS or WhatsApp

howItWorks.detail: An SMS, call or WhatsApp says you have won a car, cash, or a retailer's promotional prize. Often the brand of a genuine, well-known South African competition is used.
The framing is congratulatory, not transactional, which lowers scrutiny considerably before money is ever mentioned.
Tax, courier, insurance, clearance or a legal fee. Always modest against the prize value, which is exactly the calculation you are meant to make.
More fees follow, and along the way your ID number, address and banking details are collected for further fraud.

redFlags: You won a competition you never entered.
Any payment required to release a prize. This is illegal in South Africa.
You are asked for banking details 'to deposit the winnings'.
Contact by WhatsApp or a personal cellphone number rather than an official channel.
You are told to keep it confidential until collection.
illustrativeCase: A pensioner is phoned by a caller using a major retailer's brand, telling her she has won R250 000 in their anniversary draw. To release it she must pay a R1 750 'SARS clearance fee'. She pays. A R4 300 'courier insurance' follows, then a R7 000 'bank release'. Family intervene at R13 050.
howToProtect: Remember the rule in South African law: a promotional competition may not require any payment to claim a prize.
If you did not enter, you did not win. There is no exception to this.
Verify with the brand directly through their official website or switchboard.
Never provide banking details or an ID number to claim a prize.
Talk to older relatives about this one specifically. It targets them disproportionately.
ifYouveBeenHit: Report to the SAPS and to the brand being impersonated.
If you gave banking details or ID, alert your bank and register a SAFPS protective listing.
Report the number to your network provider.

faqs.q: Do real competitions ever charge a fee?
faqs.a: No. Under the Consumer Protection Act, requiring payment to claim a promotional prize is unlawful. A fee is definitive proof of fraud.

faqs.q: They used a real retailer's name and logo.
faqs.a: Impersonating a trusted brand is the point. Verify through the brand's own published contact details, never those given to you.
